setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Pearl Harbor Space** (2 reviews): Topical space the night before the 40th anniversary of Pearl Harbor, with Brent and Phil making airplane and falling-bomb effects; Airplane noises in the space were also inspired by planes landing near O'Hare airport [19][20]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer singles out a really nice Looks Like Rain [25]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Reviewer names To Lay Me Down as the highlight of the show [24]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer hears hints of basement-tape material in this Estimated Prophet, and says the band worked hard [17]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 other source): Some echoey effects appear in Good Lovin', and clicks and pops were removed [3]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): Listener says this Brokedown Palace stayed with them for years afterward [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-12-06.sbd.miller.108841.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 168 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1981-12-06.158845.mtx.seamons.ht150.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 163 min [3]
- **gd1981-12-06.aud.unknown.78646.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 164 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: This audience copy has good audio quality and a vintage 1981 feel [25]
- **gd1981-12-06.148950.fob.senn421.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 161 min [5]
- **gd1981-12-06.139345.aud.craigl.flac1644**: audience recording; 22 songs; 160 min [7]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has PA static in Candyman and some mic bumps in the second set [7]
- **gd81-12-06.aud.braverman.8200.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 157 min; rated 3.92/5 by 12 [9]. Said about its sound: Audience recording's quality could be better, according to the reviewer; Audience recording is somewhat rough around the edges in sound; Audience recording sounds distant from the band, with Jerry's voice thin and tiny [14][18][23]

## Around the show

- Reviewer found the Rosemont enormous on a first visit [19]
- The Horizon was a new building with poor soundproofing, so landing planes were audible; Bobby mentioned it onstage [20]
- Reviewer's first Dead show: front row center after camping outside the Horizon for three nights [20]
- Reviewer came by school bus from Ann Arbor and was surprised the floor crowd stood throughout [21]
- Reviewer traveled from Ann Arbor for a first show; the show was good, the trip wasn't [22]
- Jets passing low over the Rosemont looked like they would hit the building, unsettling the reviewer [24]
- Likened to other topical spaces, such as the Earthquake space and the Raven space [19]
- Reviewer disliked the Rosemont compared with the Uptown, where they also saw the band that year [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-12-06.sbd.miller.108841.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [1]
- **gd1981-12-06.158845.mtx.seamons.ht150.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > Soundtrack Pro > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging)… [3]. Also: Likely master reel to DAT source, starting with Tennessee Jed, per Charlie Miller's database note; Set 2 soundboard patches are lower quality than set 1's, suggesting different lineages; set 2 resembles cassette transfer [3]
- **gd1981-12-06.aud.unknown.78646.sbeok.flac16**: source: AUD Master Cass>DAT>HD-P2>Soundforge 6.0>CD Wave>FLAC Frontend>.flac [4]
- **gd1981-12-06.148950.fob.senn421.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Frank Streeter's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (TDK MA-C90) [5]. Also: Frank Streeter supplied master cassettes; Charlie Miller transferred them and coordinated the release, with Joe B. Jones helping on pitch correction; A front-of-board Sennheiser 421 source fills gaps around Candyman, Rooster, Tennessee Jed, the Samson intro, and Drums [5]
- **gd1981-12-06.139345.aud.craigl.flac1644**: taped by CraigL; transferred by AndrewF; source: UD: First Set; Richie Stankiewicz's Beyer M160's FOB. Second Set; Nakamichi CM300's w/CP4 shotguns from the floor area. Both Sets; Lead decks(s) > Sony TC-D5 >… [7]. Also: Patches from another source, ID-119584, extend Tennessee Jed and Drums [7]
- **gd81-12-06.aud.braverman.8200.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [9]
